# lib/serial module

Interrupt-driven ring-buffered UART. This page is the reference for the `lib/serial` HAL module, for firmware authors choosing and wiring it in.

## Use it

The manifest lists one example program per family, plus peer programs for extra transports where the driver has them. Build one with the repository build driver (--example names a peer), or read it as the working starting point for your own firmware.

| Family | Example | Source |
|---|---|---|
| PIC16F87XA | `serial` | [`lib/serial/examples/example_serial.c`](https://github.com/apojomovsky/epic-hal/blob/master/lib/serial/examples/example_serial.c) |
| PIC16F88X | `serial` | [`lib/serial/examples/example_serial.c`](https://github.com/apojomovsky/epic-hal/blob/master/lib/serial/examples/example_serial.c) |
| PIC18Fxx5x | `serial` | [`lib/serial/examples/example_serial.c`](https://github.com/apojomovsky/epic-hal/blob/master/lib/serial/examples/example_serial.c) |

## API

The API is documented next to the code, in the [`lib/serial` directory](https://github.com/apojomovsky/epic-hal/tree/master/lib/serial). This page does not restate it. The manifest carries no function list, so no API table is generated here yet.

## Limits

- Not built for PIC16F870, PIC16F871, PIC16F872, PIC16F873, PIC16F873A, PIC16F874, PIC16F874A, PIC16LF873A. Reason: RAM: 32-byte g_rx_buf does not fit.
